patches.reason: The wrap-up task's confirmation calls showbutton(...) in lower case, which is not a SexScript function, so Groovy failed after showing the code; every other confirmation uses showButton.

Three author errors in the tasks. The spanking dice roll getRandom(5)+1, 1 to 5, while each roll offers six numbered options, so the sixth never came up: the belt and standing upright never, and naked (5 and 6) one roll in five instead of two in six: roll getRandom(6)+1. The "you can't read" punishment saves DareWiliam.punishment, which nothing reads, while every other punishment is saved and read as the text "1" under DareWiliam.Punshishment: save that. A second code below 0 passed the code checks (only 0 was rejected) and reached Math.sqrt, which gave NaN spanks, or a wedgie code that passed with 0 wedgies: reject codes of 0 or less as the 0 code was, and take the wedgie code's square root of no less than 0, which the false-code check then rejects. Where legacy Math.sqrt() of a negative number gave NaN, TeaseScript's sqrt() stops the script; a corpus search found no other Math.sqrt(), Math.log() or fractional-exponent Math.pow() on a value that can go negative while the clock runs forward (exercise's sqrt(day - firstDay) can after the clock is set back).

Legacy bug (creator report): DW_intro reads loadInteger("DareWiliam.zip.launch.lasttime") and computes getTime() - lasttime, but no script of the package saves that key, so the read was null and Groovy failed (V2 explorer: TSR027); and DareWiliam/zip returns to DW_intro, which would send the player back to it at once. Evident intent: the intro runs the report when it last ran more than 30 seconds ago, so the report stores its launch time and a missing time means it never ran. The patch reads a missing time as 0 and makes zip.groovy save its launch time.
